The selector is `FORTRESS_LIBRARY=one` in the environment or `-Dfortress.library=one`, read once for the JVM, as probe Y built it.** The compile, the run and the harness's run step follow it, since the run step is a process that inherits the environment. **Default: so.** Way not taken: an option of each command, which every script passes on. The reason: the harness's tracks are started with their environment.

<target name="testOnly" depends="compileAll"
          description="Run specific tests (use -DtestPattern=...).">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <junit printsummary="off"
           haltonerror="off"
           haltonfailure="off"
           showoutput="yes"
           fork="true"
           maxmemory="${junitMem}"
           errorProperty="tests.failed"
           failureProperty="tests.failed">
      <classpath refid="compile.classpath"/>
      <jvmarg value="-Djava.io.tmpdir=${PF}/test-tmp" />
      <jvmarg value="${bigStack}" />
      <formatter type="plain" usefile="false"/>
      <syspropertyset>
        <propertyref prefix="plt." />
      </syspropertyset>
      <batchtest fork="true" todir="${test.results}">
        <fileset dir="${build}">
          <and>
            <filename name="**/*${testPattern}*/**" />
            <or>
              <filename name="**/*JUTest.class" />
              <filename name="**/*JUTestAll.class" />
              <filename name="**/*JxTest.class" />
            </or>
          </and>
          <exclude name="**/*$*.class"/>
        </fileset>
      </batchtest>
    </junit>
    <delete dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <fail message="Tests expected to pass are failing!" if="tests.failed"/>
  </target>

  <target name="test" depends="compileAll, testFast, testLibrary"
          description="Clean, compile everything, and run all unit and system tests.">
  </target>

  <!-- The per-corpus targets run their corpus as testFast's tracks do
....
  <target name="testUntil"
          depends="compileAll"
          description="Run all unit and system tests expected to pass, halting on any errors or failures.">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <junit printsummary="on"
           haltonerror="on"
           haltonfailure="on"
           showoutput="yes"
           fork="true"
           maxmemory="${junitMem}"
           errorProperty="tests.failed"
           failureProperty="tests.failed">
      <classpath refid="compile.classpath"/>
      <jvmarg value="-Djava.io.tmpdir=${PF}/test-tmp" />
      <formatter type="plain" usefile="true"/>
      <batchtest fork="true" todir="${test.results}">
        <fileset dir="${build}">
          <include name="**/*JUTest.class"/>
          <include name="**/*JUTests.class"/>

          <!-- Do not run the interpreter tests here. Only run the interpreter
               tests during nightly and CruiseControl testing. -->
          <exclude name="**/TopLevelEnvGenJUTest.class"/>
          <exclude name="**/NightlyCompilerJUTest.class"/>

          <exclude name="**/*$*.class"/>
          <exclude name="**/SyntaxAbstractionJUTestAll.class"/>
          <exclude name="**/ObjectExpressionVisitorJUTest.class"/>
          <exclude name="**/tools/AstJUTest.class"/>
        </fileset>
      </batchtest>
    </junit>
    <delete dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <fail message="Tests expected to pass are failing!" if="tests.failed"/>
  </target>

  <target name="testParser" depends="compileAll"
          description="Run parser tests to debug CruiseControl (Temporary debugging target)">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <junit printsummary="on"
           haltonerror="off"
           haltonfailure="off"
           showoutput="yes"
           fork="true"
           maxmemory="${junitMem}"
           errorProperty="tests.failed"
           failureProperty="tests.failed">
      <classpath refid="compile.classpath"/>
      <jvmarg value="-Djava.io.tmpdir=${PF}/test-tmp" />
      <formatter type="plain" usefile="true"/>
      <batchtest fork="true" todir="${junit.dir}">
        <formatter type="brief" usefile="false" />
        <formatter type="xml" />
        <fileset dir="${build}">
          <include name="**/ParserJUTest.class"/>
          <exclude name="**/CompilerJUTest.class"/>

          <!-- TopLevelEnvGen tests are broken, comment out for now -->
          <exclude name="**/TopLevelEnvGenJUTest.class"/>
          <exclude name="**/*$*.class"/>
          <exclude name="**/SyntaxAbstractionJUTestAll.class"/>
          <exclude name="**/ObjectExpressionVisitorJUTest.class"/>
          <exclude name="**/tools/AstJUTest.class"/>

        </fileset>
      </batchtest>
    </junit>
    <delete dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <fail message="Tests expected to pass are failing!" if="tests.failed"/>
  </target>

  <target name="testCruiseControl" depends="compileAll"
          description="Run all unit and system tests expected to pass.">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <junit printsummary="on"
           haltonerror="off"
           haltonfailure="off"
           showoutput="yes"
           fork="true"
           maxmemory="${junitMem}"
           errorProperty="tests.failed"

content.content:
<!--
       The caches and the implementation.

       The caches (${cache0}, ${cache1}, ${cacheOne}, and the private ones the tests use)
       hold what the implementation made from Fortress code: parsed and
       analysed ASTs, walk's rewritten ASTs and environments, compiled jars,
       native wrappers.  Fortress checks an entry against its Fortress sources,
       by date, and never against the implementation, so the build decides
       whether the caches still belong to the implementation:

       - ${build}/implementation.stamp is a SHA-1 over the implementation as it
         runs: every file of ${build}, ${PF}/third_party and bin, and
         default_repository/configuration, each with its relative path, and
         the JDK's version.  compileAll writes it last, after a successful
         build, and deletes it first.
       - A caches folder holds the stamp of the implementation it belongs to.
         At its end, compileAll keeps a caches folder only if that stamp equals
         the new build's: the implementation is byte for byte the one that
         filled it.  Otherwise it deletes the folder and starts it again, empty,
         with the new stamp.
       - ${build}/implementation.sources is a SHA-1 over what the build is made
         from: ${PF}/src (class files aside), ${PF}/astgen, ${PF}/third_party,
         bin, build.xml and default_repository/configuration, and the JDK's
         version.  When it differs at the start of compileAll, the build may
         change the implementation, so the caches are deleted before anything
         compiles, as cleanCache did here before: a build that then fails
         leaves no caches behind.  So are they when the build directory is no
         longer what the last build left (something else compiled into it).
       - scalac runs only when its inputs (the sources) or the build directory
         differ from what the last successful build left; for the same inputs
         its output is the same, byte for byte.

       ant cleanCache deletes the caches whatever their stamp; ant clean
       deletes the build too.
  -->

....
      </fingerprint>
    </sequential>
  </macrodef>

  <!-- Keep the caches folder @{dir} if it holds the stamp @{stamp};
       otherwise delete it, and, if it is a repository's caches folder,
       start it again, empty, with that stamp. -->
  <macrodef name="stampCache">
    <attribute name="dir"/>
    <attribute name="stamp"/>
    <sequential>
      <local name="cache.stamp"/>
      <local name="cache.kept"/>
      <local name="cache.parent"/>
      <local name="cache.restart"/>
      <loadfile property="cache.stamp" srcFile="@{dir}/implementation.stamp"
                quiet="true">
        <filterchain><striplinebreaks/></filterchain>
      </loadfile>
      <condition property="cache.kept">
        <equals arg1="${cache.stamp}" arg2="@{stamp}"/>
      </condition>
      <dirname property="cache.parent" file="@{dir}"/>
      <condition property="cache.restart">
        <and>
          <not><isset property="cache.kept"/></not>
          <available file="${cache.parent}/configuration"/>
        </and>
      </condition>
      <delete dir="@{dir}" unless:set="cache.kept"/>
      <mkdir dir="@{dir}" if:set="cache.restart"/>
      <echo file="@{dir}/implementation.stamp" message="@{stamp}${line.separator}"
            if:set="cache.restart"/>
      <echo message="Caches @{dir} kept" if:set="cache.kept"/>
      <echo message="Caches @{dir} started again, empty" if:set="cache.restart"/>
    </sequential>
  </macrodef>

  <!-- Read what the last successful build left, delete its stamps (they
       come back at the end of a successful compileAll), and delete the caches
       now if the sources or the build directory changed since that build, or
       the caches do not belong to it. -->
  <target name="checkCaches" depends="init">
    <sourcesFingerprint property="sources.start"/>
    <implementationFingerprint property="implementation.found"/>

api For
import FortressAst.{...}

object Unreachable extends UncheckedException end
grammar ForLoop extends {Expression, Identifier}
    Expr |:= for b:forStart => <[ b ]>
    forStart :Expr:=
        i:Id <- e:Expr d:doFront      => <[ ((e).loop(fn i => d)) ]>
      | e:Expr d:doFront              => <[ if e then d end ]>
      | i:Id <- e:Expr , b:forStart   => <[ ((e).loop(fn i => b)) ]>
      | e:Expr , b:forStart           => <[ if e then b end ]>
    doFront :Expr:=
        a:atomicFront => <[ a ]>
      | at e:Expr a:atomicFront => <[ a ]>
    atomicFront :Expr:=
        do d:doBody => <[ d ]>
      | atomic do d:doBody =>
        <[ label atomicBlock
               while true do
                   try
                       result = tryatomic d
                       exit atomicBlock with result
                   catch e
                       TryAtomicFailure => ()
                   end
               end
               throw Unreachable
           end atomicBlock
        ]>
    doBody :Expr:=
        end => <[ () ]>
      | block:Expr end => <[ block ]>
end
end

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

<!-- The per-corpus targets run their corpus as testFast's tracks do
       (fastTrack, below: private caches, the same JVM settings), after an
       incremental build. Each starts its own tracks' caches empty and leaves
       the other tracks' and default_repository/caches alone. -->
  <target name ="testCompiler" depends="compileAll"
          description="Test the native code generator: testFast's compiler and othercompiler tracks">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}/fast-compiler"/>
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}/fast-othercompiler"/>
    <parallel threadcount="2">
      <fastTrack id="compiler">
        <include name="**/CompilerJUTest.class"/>
      </fastTrack>
      <fastTrack id="othercompiler">
        <include name="**/OtherCompilerJUTest.class"/>
      </fastTrack>
    </parallel>
    <delete dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <fail message="Tests expected to pass are failing!" if="tests.failed"/>
  </target>

  <target name ="testOtherCompiler" depends="compileAll"
          description="Test the native code generator on other_compiler_tests: testFast's othercompiler track">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}/fast-othercompiler"/>
    <fastTrack id="othercompiler">
      <include name="**/OtherCompilerJUTest.class"/>
    </fastTrack>
    <delete dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <fail message="Tests expected to pass are failing!" if="tests.failed"/>
  </target>

  <target name ="testLibrary" depends="compileAll"
          description="Test the compiler libraries: testFast's library track">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}/fast-library"/>
    <fastTrack id="library">
      <include name="**/LibraryJUTest.class"/>
    </fastTrack>
    <delete dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <fail message="Tests expected to pass are failing!" if="tests.failed"/>
  </target>

  <target name ="testOneLibrary" depends="compileAll"
          description="Test the compiled path against the one library: testFast's onelibrary track">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}/fast-onelibrary"/>
    <fastTrack id="onelibrary" library="one">
      <include name="**/OneLibraryJUTest.class"/>
    </fastTrack>
    <delete dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <fail message="Tests expected to pass are failing!" if="tests.failed"/>
  </target>

  <target name ="testQuick" depends="compileAll"
  <target name="testFast" depends="compileAll"
          description="Run all unit and system tests expected to pass.">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}"/>
    <!-- The three big suites each dominate a track; everything else shares
         the fourth. Wall clock is the slowest single suite, not the sum. -->
    <parallel threadcount="4">
      <fastTrack id="compiler">
       heap and stack that explorations/experiment/env.sh exports.
       FORTRESS_LIBRARY is pinned too, to the track's library attribute:
       "one" where the track compiles against the one library, as the
       onelibrary track does, and empty, the compiler's prelude, for the
       others, whatever the shell that called ant exports. -->
  <macrodef name="fastTrack">
    <attribute name="id"/>
    <attribute name="library" default=""/>
    <element name="tests" implicit="yes"/>
    <sequential>
      <mkdir dir="${test.results}/fast-@{id}"/>
      <junit printsummary="on"
             haltonerror="off"
             haltonfailure="off"
             showoutput="yes"
             fork="true"
             maxmemory="${junitMem}"
             errorProperty="tests.failed"
             failureProperty="tests.failed">
        <classpath refid="compile.classpath"/>
        <sysproperty key="fortress.junit.reset" value="false"/>
        <sysproperty key="fortress.caches" value="${test.caches}/fast-@{id}"/>
        <env key="FORTRESS_CACHES" value="${test.caches}/fast-@{id}"/>
        <env key="FORTRESS_LIBRARY" value="@{library}"/>
        <env key="FORTRESS_THREADS" value="4"/>
        <env key="JAVA_FLAGS"
             value="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=${basedir}/${PF}/test-tmp"/>
        <jvmarg value="-Djava.io.tmpdir=${PF}/test-tmp" />
        <jvmarg value="${bigStack}" />
        <formatter type="plain" usefile="true"/>
        <batchtest fork="true" todir="${test.results}/fast-@{id}">
          <fileset dir="${build}">
            <tests/>
          </fileset>
        </batchtest>
      </junit>
    </sequential>
  </macrodef>
